name: Congenital Anomaly of the Great Arteries

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Congenital Great Artery Anomaly Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Anatomical confirmation of abnormal origin or course of the great arteries by imaging
Presence of central cyanosis in the neonatal period
Echocardiographic evidence of transposition or malposition of the aorta and pulmonary artery
Characteristic systolic murmur detected on auscultation
Electrocardiographic abnormalities consistent with right ventricular hypertrophy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of anatomical confirmation of great artery anomaly by imaging plus clinical evidence of cyanosis or echocardiographic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on imaging and clinical presentation in the neonatal period.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of lips and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia
Bounding or weak pulses depending on associated defects

common.notes: Rapid breathing due to compromised oxygenation
Heard on auscultation due to turbulent blood flow

occasional.notes: Shortness of breath on feeding or activity
Irregular heartbeats due to cardiac structural abnormalities
Enlarged liver secondary to congestive heart failure
Swelling due to right heart failure

rare.notes: Stroke or hypoxic brain injury secondary to cardiac anomaly
Elevated pulmonary artery pressure from chronic shunting

imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating abnormal great artery origins
Cardiac MRI or CT angiography confirming arterial anatomy
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly or pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No single gene identified; may be associated with chromosomal anomalies such as 22q11 deletion syndrome
other: Pulse oximetry with decreased oxygen saturation

distinguishingFeatures: Ventricular septal defect with overriding aorta
Single arterial trunk arising from the heart
Absence of separate aorta and pulmonary artery

redFlags: Severe central cyanosis unresponsive to oxygen therapy
Signs of congestive heart failure in neonate
Sudden onset of arrhythmia or cardiac arrest
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Maron BJ, et al. Clinical Cardiology: Current Practice Guidelines. 2022.
Orphanet: Congenital anomaly of the great arteries. ORPHA:98724.
